title: Given Facts II
author: UncleLogic
rules:
Given Facts II is a math-and-logic follow-up to my original Given Facts puzzle.

This time, instead of general-knowledge questions, all clues are based on basic mathematics, number properties, and logical relationships.

Many clues have more than one possible answer. The challenge is to use the numerical clues, their intersections, and standard Sudoku deductions together to determine the correct digits.

No outside trivia or advanced mathematical knowledge is required.

Sudoku:

Place the digits 1–9 in every row, column, and 3×3 box, with no repeats.

Fact Entries:

Each outlined group of cells corresponds to a numbered Across or Down clue. Read Across entries from left to right and Down entries from top to bottom to form a number.

Every entry must satisfy its corresponding clue, and all digits must obey the Sudoku rules. The number in parentheses indicates the length of the entry.

There are no ordinary given digits.

Across:

A1 (3) — This number is 5 greater than A8.

A2 (2) — The digits decrease and sum to 11.

A3 (2) — Reverse the digits of A5.

A4 (3) — This number is twice D7.

A5 (2) — A two-digit prime below 50 whose digits sum to 10.

A6 (2) — The digits sum to 14.

A7 (3) — Each digit is 2 greater than the previous digit. The number is below 500.

A8 (3) — A multiple of 11 between 850 and 900.

A9 (3) — This number is 11 times A2.

A10 (2) — An odd two-digit number whose digits sum to 10.

A11 (3) — The digits strictly decrease and sum to 10.

A12 (3) — The digits strictly increase and multiply to 24.

Down:

D1 (3) — A three-digit perfect cube between 200 and 750.

D2 (3) — The digits strictly decrease and sum to 22.

D3 (4) — Four consecutive increasing digits, forming a number below 5000.

D4 (2) — The two digits multiply to 18.

D5 (3) — A multiple of 18 between 300 and 350.

D6 (2) — A two-digit perfect square below 50.

D7 (2) — The two digits sum to 16.

D8 (2) — What is 9 × 9?

Solve in SudokuPad

About Given Facts II:

This is the second proof of concept for a potential numerical crossword and Sudoku hybrid.

The original explored general-knowledge clues. This version focuses entirely on mathematical and logical deductions. I'd especially appreciate feedback on whether the interaction between the clues and Sudoku feels enjoyable, and which approach you prefer.

I hope you enjoy it!

More puzzles by me can be found at UncleLogic.com.
